subject: Usage discrepancy adjudication and credits — post-renewal
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected post-renewal charges — August usage spike

Marcus —

Hope you’re well. We signed the renewal on July 15 (12-month committed tier) and noticed a ~47% spike in tokens billed for the month of August compared to our committed baseline. That resulted in a one-off overage charge on our August invoice that we weren't expecting.

I’ve attached a PDF with the line-item usage by route and model (acme_usage_detail_aug2026.pdf). Can you help us understand whether this is a metering issue or legitimate burst activity that should be billed? If legitimate, can we discuss a credit schedule or an amortized top-up instead of a single large invoice?

We’d like to resolve before month-end billing closes.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Finance Operations
Acme Cloud Solutions

Attachment: acme_usage_detail_aug2026.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal charges — August usage spike

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for flagging and for the usage PDF — that was helpful. I pulled the raw ingress logs and the spike looks concentrated on two endpoints: /chat/batch-embed and /routes/generate-large where a small set of jobs ran with much longer sequences than historical averages. Early hypothesis: a data-import process at Acme reprocessed a backlog and hit the API without the intended rate limiter.

Proposed immediate steps:
- We’ll freeze further automated billing for the disputed period while we investigate (no new adjudication until we agree).
- Redwood to provide a reconciliation workbook with per-route token counts and recommended one-time amortized credit options.
- If the traffic is user-initiated legitimate usage, we can offer a one-time credit equal to 50% of the overage and an option to spread remaining overage across next two invoices.

I’ve looped in Aditya (account lead) and Laura (customer success billing) to coordinate the proposal. Can you confirm whether the backlog import was intentional and whether Acme can accept an amortized adjustment?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 26KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T10:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal charges — August usage spike

Samantha, Marcus —

Following Marcus’s note, we ran the reconciliation against token-level logs and attached a summarized workbook (see proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx). Key points:
- Overage quantity: 1,264,780 tokens above committed baseline for August.
- Recommended remediation: 60% credit on the overage (given the one-off nature and our platform detection limitations) + spread remaining 40% over next two invoices (20% each).
- If Acme confirms the backlog was intentional and frequent, we’ll propose an amendment to the committed tier for future months instead of credits.

If you’re comfortable, we can draft a short amendment (one paragraph) to the MSA to record the credit + amortization and push a corrected August invoice. Laura — once Samantha confirms, can your billing team prepare the invoice adjustment and updated billing schedule?

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-08-25T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal charges — August usage spike

Aditya / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick analysis. The spike was from an internal data re-ingest that should not have hit production; it was a mistake. Acme is comfortable with an amortized approach but we’d like the corrected invoice in September with the credit applied and the remaining balance split across Sep/Oct.

Please send the draft amendment for legal to sign and the corrected invoice when ready. Also include a short note in the invoice explaining the credit and amortization schedule so our accounts payable team can process it.

Samantha Ortiz
Finance Operations
Acme Cloud Solutions

Attachment: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal charges — August usage spike

Samantha —

We’ll take care of this. Actions we completed today:
1) Drafted a one-paragraph amendment capturing a one-time 60% credit on the August overage, with the remaining 40% amortized 20% Sep / 20% Oct. Draft attached: draft-amendment-aug28.docx.
2) Billing will void the August overage line and issue a corrected invoice by Sept 1 showing the applied credit and the two amortized charges on Sep/Oct invoices (reference HS-ACME-317).
3) I’ve added a short billing note for AP to the invoice and included the token-level reconciliation as backup.

Please confirm acceptance and I’ll route the amendment to your legal and finalize the invoice flow.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: draft-amendment-aug28.docx (document, 12KB)
